extracted.intended_audience: journalists, data journalists, journalism students, newsroom editors and managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for producing data-driven journalism: sourcing, cleaning, analyzing, visualizing, publishing and measuring data stories, plus related ethical and methodological considerations. Useful for practitioners and students planning data-driven reporting or designing newsroom workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven journalism definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism based on the filtering and analysis of large data sets for the purpose of creating or elevating a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises blending journalism with data visualization, computer science and statistics; the primary goal is telling stories based on the data and transforming findings into journalistic writing to make complex situations understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core workflow (digging, filtering, visualizing, making a story)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data-driven journalism is primarily a workflow that consists of digging deep into data by scraping, cleansing and structuring it; filtering by mining for specific information; visualizing; and making a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each stage is distinct and iterative: digging may require scraping/OCR, filtering uses analytical/mining techniques, visualization exposes patterns, and narrative connects findings to people and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-phase process: Find, Clean, Visualize, Publish, Distribute, Measure
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic six-phase model splitting the transformation of raw data into stories into: Find, Clean, Visualize, Publish, Distribute, Measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the phases as a pipeline for project planning; practical tools and practices differ per phase (e.g., scrapers for Find; OpenRefine for Clean; tableau/JS libraries for Visualize; CMS integration for Publish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding data / sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate data via governmental databases (data.gov, data.gov.uk, World Bank API), Freedom of Information requests, web scraping, OCR on PDFs, or crowdsourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose sources appropriate to jurisdiction and story; use scrapers (WebScraper, Import.io, etc.), OCR when data is locked in PDFs; consider FOI/requests and leaks as sources; document provenance for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning and preparing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Data often needs cleaning, structuring and transformation before analysis or visualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to remove/handle extraneous data points, reformat rows/columns, normalize fields; tools include OpenRefine, Data Wrangler, Google Spreadsheets. Data cleaning is essential to produce reliable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualizing data: meaningful and relevant visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Create visual displays (static or interactive) that reveal patterns and help readers understand the significance of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate chart types and levels of interactivity; use tools and libraries (Tableau Public, Many Eyes, RGraph, JS libraries, HTML5 canvas) and follow published tutorials/guides to ensure visualizations are clear and truthful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing data stories and attaching data
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate visuals into articles, attach the underlying data to stories, and (for specials) create dossiers that combine multiple visualizations and articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider CMS limitations (many are date-post based) and build specially coded pages where needed; attaching the data enables verification and invites further analysis by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributing data and enabling access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to datasets used so others can investigate, reproduce or build upon the work; think of distribution platforms as marketplaces for datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host or link to data (Buzzdata, ScraperWiki, Timetric, etc.); promoting dataset access fosters community scrutiny and can start new cycles of interrogation leading to more stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring impact ethically
rubrics_metrics.description: Track how often a dataset or visualization is viewed while being mindful that extensive user tracking can be problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer non-intrusive measurement tools (e.g., PixelPing by ProPublica/DocumentCloud) and avoid collecting user data for unrelated marketing uses; be transparent about tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Critically examine data sources, completeness, accuracy and format; data may have omissions or be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should include assessment of data quality and may themselves become stories (e.g., refusals to provide data, poor formatting). Note limitations and uncertainties in published reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling: explain as well as show
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform findings from data into narrative that explains what the findings mean from the perspective of affected people, not just showing patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid producing outputs that merely 'show the problem' without explaining it; good productions allow drilling down (personalized detail) and zooming out (big picture) so readers both relate and understand context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust and public service role
rubrics_metrics.description: Data journalism should aim to be verifiable, trustworthy, relevant and easy to remember, helping media shift 'from attention to trust'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat trust as a scarce resource: rigorous verification, transparent methods, and sharing data increase credibility and position newsrooms as trusted data hubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy and selecting appropriate story type
rubrics_metrics.description: Different project types exist (e.g., just the facts, data-based news stories, local data telling stories, analysis/background, deep dive investigations; and forms like tables, static maps, dynamic maps, timelines, infographics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the type and form of data story that matches the editorial aim and the data available; taxonomies (Megan Knight, Simon Rogers, Martha Kang, Veglis & Bratsas) can guide scope and format decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative data journalism standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative data journalism combines data methods with investigative reporting to research large textual or financial datasets and sometimes secret/non-open data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require advanced analytics, legal/ethical considerations around leaked or restricted data, and rigorous verification; examples include large-scale leak projects (e.g., Wikileaks, Panama Papers) and Pulitzer-winning work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of open data and open-source tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Many data-driven stories begin with open data and are produced using open-source tools; openness aids reproducibility and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor publishing or linking to underlying data and using open tools where practical; this supports verification and wider reuse of datasets and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactivity design: transmissional, consultational, conversational
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive visualizations can be classified by how they present data: transmissional (one-way), consultational (allow users to query), or conversational (support user interaction and feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the appropriate interactivity level based on story goals, audience needs and data complexity; interactive layers should enhance comprehension, not confuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required technical and statistical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Data journalists need skills to find data (e.g., MySQL, Python), interrogate data (understanding jargon and statistics), and visualize/mash using tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage skill development in scraping, databases, scripting, statistical literacy and visualization libraries; collaboration across newsroom roles can combine different competencies.
